setlist.title: Beat It on Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (4 reviews): Opening Half-Step starts shakily, but Franklin's Tower finishes strongly; Half Step into Franklin's is called decent, with the show declining afterward [10][13][15][16]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Let It Grow closes the first set with energy; Jerry plays hot licks in Let It Grow [10][14]
- **Samson & Delilah** (2 reviews): Samson & Delilah features strong Jerry guitar playing; Reviewer found Samson & Delilah smoking, knowing it from Peter, Paul and Mary [14][16]
- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Reviewer says Brent actually quit playing during Good Lovin', and the band nearly stopped; Good Lovin' and the Don't Ease Me In finish redeem the show; Black Peter and Around & Around are limp [13][20]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Jerry sounds relaxed and happy, and his Candyman vocal is especially praised [12]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Brent scat-sings during Rooster, and also backs Bobby on the He's Gone chorus [15]
- **Never Trust a Woman** (1 review): Second set shines throughout, with Never Trust a Woman singled out and everything after Space strong [10]
- **Around & Around** (1 review): Brent holds an extended high organ note during Around & Around [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-04-11.137976.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd82-04-11.fob-senn421-wise.sacks.6959.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 170 min; rated 3.22/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: The audience tape is listenable; Both set openers are hard to hear as the tapers fumble with equipment and raise the stand; later improves; Recorded from ninth row center; some bumps, but overall a very listenable audience recording [14][15][20]
- **gd1982-04-11.155627.set2.beyer.m88.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 12 songs; 94 min [8]
- **gd1982-04-11.sbd.miller.108852.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 166 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first Dead show; they went on to attend 110 more [11]
- Brent plays an angry, hellacious solo after a gritty scat vocal [18]
- Reviewer judges the second set among the worst they saw, and says the next night's show was far better [13]
- Jerry played two solo acoustic shows at the Capitol Theatre in Passaic, NJ the night before, after Rochester; this show is pretty good but not tour's best [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-04-11.137976.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 source matrix by Dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:108852), SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k),Transfer Info:Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional… [1]
- **gd82-04-11.fob-senn421-wise.sacks.6959.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [3]
- **gd1982-04-11.155627.set2.beyer.m88.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Beyer M88 mics > unknown deck; Jim Vita's 1st generation cassette (Maxell XLIIS 90) [8]. Also: A Nakamichi 300 source from Tim Friend and Joe Morrone supplies a 6:46 patch in Drums [8]
- **gd1982-04-11.sbd.miller.108852.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-04-11 Nassau Coliseum, Uniondale, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-04-11-nassau-coliseum-uniondale-ny-usa/) [24]
